Consider a continuous function $f$ defined on the closed interval $-10\le x\le 5.$ The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above for the region $-7\le x\le 5,$ and consists of two line segments and an arc of a semi-circle centered at $(-4,1)$ with radius $3.$ It is known that the point $(-5,1+2\sqrt{2})$ is on the graph of $f.$

Earlier part 1:

What is the area of a circle of radius $3?$

                                        $9\pi$

feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of a circle is

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}.
$$

Substituting the radius $r=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\pi \cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =9\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
